title: Montréal
intro: Two nights. Good food, independent shops, and a little unusual architecture. Here is the route.
booking: Book Le Germain’s Signature Two Queen Beds room and L’Express for Saturday at 7 PM. Nothing is reserved yet.
assumptions: Assumes driving from Boston and sharing one room with two beds. All times are Eastern. Recheck hours before leaving.

days.label: Friday night
days.title: Arrive, check in, get some poutine.
days.summary: Keep the first night easy. Park at the hotel and leave the car there for the weekend.

blocks.title: Check in at Le Germain
blocks.text: Drop your bags and settle in. Tell the hotel you will arrive late.

blocks.title: La Banquise
blocks.text: Take a taxi for a classic poutine. Share one if you only want a late snack, then head back to the hotel.

days.label: Saturday
days.title: Mile End → the river → a proper dinner.
days.summary: Walk within each neighborhood. Take taxis for the longer transfers.

blocks.title: Bagels and coffee in Mile End
blocks.text: Taxi to St-Viateur Bagel for a hot sesame bagel, then walk to Café Olimpico for coffee.

blocks.title: Browse Bernard, then visit LVNEA
blocks.text: Start at Bref for ceramics and design objects. Walk east to LVNEA and try a few locally made botanical perfumes.

nearby.text: Books and graphic novels on Bernard.
A wider selection of niche fragrances on Hutchison.

blocks.title: Lunch at Schwartz’s
blocks.text: Walk south for a medium-fat smoked-meat sandwich, mustard, and a pickle. Use the takeaway counter if the sit-down line is long.

blocks.title: Go see Habitat 67
blocks.text: Taxi to Avenue Pierre-Dupuy to see Moshe Safdie’s stacked housing experiment from the public street. This is an exterior visit, so no tour booking is needed. Stay out of the private residential walkways.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel
blocks.text: Taxi back, warm up, and take a break before dinner. If the weather is miserable, skip the exposed Habitat stop and come back earlier.

blocks.title: Dinner at L’Express
blocks.text: A proper French bistro evening. Get a main each, share a starter or dessert, and keep the wine order modest. Allow CAD 75–110 each before tax and tip.

blocks.title: One cocktail at Cloakroom
blocks.text: Taxi over for one drink tailored to your tastes. Ask the price before ordering rare spirits. It is walk-in only; if there is a long queue, finish the evening at the hotel.

days.label: Sunday
days.title: Old Montréal, then home.
days.summary: A compact morning. Leave Montréal at 1:30 PM to protect the 10 PM Boston target.

blocks.title: Check out, then coffee at Crew
blocks.text: Leave bags with the hotel and taxi to Crew Collective & Café. Have coffee and a pastry beneath the old bank ceiling.

blocks.title: Place d’Armes and the old streets
blocks.text: Walk to Notre-Dame’s square, then follow Saint-Paul east to L’Empreinte for Québec-made ceramics and craft. Continue to the waterfront for a short walk.

blocks.title: An early lunch at Olive et Gourmando
blocks.text: Walk back along Saint-Paul for a sandwich. Take it to go if there is a queue; do not wait for a brunch table.

blocks.title: Collect bags and the car
blocks.text: Taxi back to Le Germain. Arrange the car retrieval before you sit down to lunch.

blocks.title: Leave for Boston
blocks.text: Check live navigation and US-bound border waits that morning. Leave earlier if conditions require it. The 10 PM arrival is a target, not a guarantee.

practical.title: Two things to reserve
practical.text: Le Germain, Signature Two Queen Beds. L’Express, Saturday 7 PM: +1 514 845-5333. Everything else is walk-in or an exterior visit.

practical.title: Getting around
practical.text: Keep the car at the hotel. Walk in Mile End and Old Montréal; use taxis for Habitat 67, hotel breaks, and evening transfers.

practical.title: The return drive
practical.text: Leave at 1:30 PM Sunday. Check live traffic and the US entry queue at Highgate Springs before lunch.
